answers.question: What do 'created', 'uploaded', 'finalized' mean?
answers.answer: CREATED is written and immediately overwritten to UPLOADING in the SAME createEvidence transaction, so no committed row normally rests in CREATED (except adapters that reserve differently). UPLOADING = a key has been reserved and a presigned PUT will be issued after commit; it says nothing about bytes. UPLOADED is a dead enum value: no writer sets it anywhere in services/api, services/worker or packages (only readers). 'Finalized' = SIGNED, written by the single finalize claim after the server HEADs and fully GET-streams every original (by the HEAD's VersionId), computes SHA-256, signs the fingerprint and requests an RFC3161 token, all inside one transaction. REPORTED = a report version has been committed by the worker.

answers.question: When do original bytes become immutable, by what call?
answers.answer: Only when S3_OBJECT_LOCK_ENABLED=true. Then the Object Lock mode + retain-until are part of the presigned PutObject command (so every uploaded VERSION is locked at PUT time), CreateMultipartUpload carries the same defaults, and after the finalize commit applyRetentionOrThrow issues PutObjectRetention BY KEY (no VersionId), then HEADs BY KEY and snapshots the result onto the row. Before that commit nothing prevents a new version being written at the same key: the presigned PUT URL stays valid for up to 600s (clamped <=900s) after issuance, and the part-presign route re-issues a PUT URL for an existing part key while status is not SIGNED/REPORTED. Immutability of 'what was signed' therefore rests on the recorded storageVersionId (added 2026-09-29), not on the key. No native legal hold is ever written (removed deliberately).

answers.question: When does chain of custody begin?
answers.answer: At row creation, before any byte exists: EVIDENCE_CREATED, IDENTITY_SNAPSHOT_RECORDED and UPLOAD_AUTHORIZED are appended in the createEvidence transaction. Byte-level custody (UPLOAD_COMPLETED with server fileSha256, SIGNATURE_APPLIED, TIMESTAMP_*) is appended inside the finalize transaction; EVIDENCE_LOCKED or STORAGE_PROTECTION_UNAVAILABLE after commit (can be missing entirely if the post-commit step throws).

answers.question: Which states are terminal?
answers.answer: status: FAILED_HASH_MISMATCH is terminal by intent (finalize refuses it; integrity helper only enters it) but the report-commit writer can overwrite it in a race (STATEMACHINE-02). REPORTED is sticky (no writer moves it backward except to FAILED_HASH_MISMATCH). lifecycleState: DESTROYED is terminal by table (governance-lifecycle.ts:63) but writers are check-then-write (STATEMACHINE-04). Destruction never changes `status`, so a destroyed tombstone still says SIGNED/REPORTED; readers must consult lifecycleState/destroyedAtUtc. No terminal state exists for abandoned uploads: CREATED/UPLOADING rows are never moved anywhere.

answers.question: What happens to partial records / who cleans abandoned multipart uploads?
answers.answer: Evidence rows stuck in CREATED/UPLOADING are never transitioned or deleted; services/worker/src/orphan-scan.ts is explicitly read-only (logs counts). capture-reaper.ts only expires DRAFT CaptureSession rows and 'Never deletes or modifies any Evidence'. Single-shot PUT objects uploaded but never completed stay in the bucket indefinitely (and, with Object Lock, locked for the retention window). Native S3 multipart uploads are aborted by reapStaleMultipartUploads, which is DB-driven (only sessions with multipart_upload_id recorded) and reachable only from POST /v1/ops/reconcile (cron-secret; no in-repo scheduler). No bucket lifecycle rule (AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload) exists in the repo. An S3 multipart created by initiate whose DB persist UPDATE matches 0 rows (concurrent initiate) is not aborted because $executeRawUnsafe returns 0 instead of throwing (upload-session.service.ts:1460-1486).

answers.question: Can the DB claim success while storage is incomplete?
answers.answer: Not for SIGNED: the finalize tx HEADs and fully hashes every object before the claim. But (a) the post-commit retention/lock-snapshot step can throw after SIGNED is committed, returning an error to the client while the DB says SIGNED, with no lock snapshot and no EVIDENCE_LOCKED/STORAGE_PROTECTION_UNAVAILABLE event and no OTS/report request from this call (reconcilers later cover OTS and report, nothing re-applies/records the lock); (b) completeStorageMultipart persists completion then creates the bridge EvidencePart in a swallowed try/catch — the storage object exists without a part row. Both are recorded in STATEMACHINE-05.

answers.question: Can storage succeed while DB failed?
answers.answer: Yes, by design and without cleanup: any uploaded original whose /complete never succeeds (client abandons, tx timeout, checklist refusal, EVIDENCE_TOO_LARGE after hashing) remains in the bucket under evidence/{id}/...; the row stays UPLOADING forever. Destruction enumerates evidence/{id}/ by prefix, so trashing+destroying the row would reach them, but nothing trashes stuck rows.

answers.question: Which bytes are hashed, and is the multipart assembled object re-hashed server-side?
answers.answer: The ORIGINAL stored bytes, streamed from S3 (never a transformed derivative). Single file: fileSha256 = SHA-256 of the object version the HEAD described. Multi-part (EvidencePart rows): each part hashed; fileSha256 = sha256(partHashes.join('|')) and multipartManifestSha256 = sha256(partHashes.join('\n')). A native S3 multipart object IS re-hashed server-side as a whole object by completeEvidence (it is bridged as an EvidencePart); the ETag is never used as a hash (fingerprint etag: null). The worker re-hashes the same versions at report time and compares to fileSha256.

answers.question: Is the version ID persisted and used?
answers.answer: Persisted since 2026-09-29 (Evidence.storageVersionId, EvidencePart.storageVersionId) from the HEAD used for hashing. Used by the worker re-hash, the authenticated original download (evidence.routes.ts:11517) and per-part download (:6236). NOT used by buildPublicEvidenceContent viewUrl (evidence.routes.ts:3767, :3906 — the params type has no version field), by applyObjectRetention / post-commit HEAD snapshot, by archive-tier CopyObject/Restore, nor by verifyCompletedObject. See STATEMACHINE-03.

answers.question: Object key tenant binding; can a client choose the key?
answers.answer: No. Keys are server-built: evidence/{serverUUID}/original-{sanitizedBasename}, evidence/{id}/parts/{NNN}-{sanitizedName}, evidence/{id}/multipart/{sessionUUID}/object (UUID-validated). The client influences only the sanitized filename suffix. Keys are bound to the evidence id, not the team; tenant isolation is by authorization before presign.

answers.question: Destruction path and download after destruction
answers.answer: Single executor: claim (CAS) -> eligibility recompute -> inventory every version under row keys + evidence-owned prefixes -> refuse if any version retained/held -> DeleteObject by VersionId -> re-list and refuse certificate on survivors -> tombstone (storageKey null) + child rows deleted + EVIDENCE_PURGED. Downloads after destruction have no key to presign. Residual risk: a report commit racing the executor can recreate reports/{id}/ objects and a Report row after the certificate (STATEMACHINE-02).

answers.question: Presigned URL TTLs
answers.answer: Evidence/part PUT: 600s requested, clamped to [60,900] by S3_PRESIGN_EXPIRES_SECONDS logic. Multipart UploadPart: default 300s, cap 900s. GET (download/view): 600s. Sessions: 1h default expiry.

answers.question: Integrity-rejection path
answers.answer: rejectEvidenceIntegrity is called ONLY from the report worker's prepareReportArtifacts (processor.ts:2384 multipart, :2423 single). The declared sources 'worker.reconciler' and 'api.completion' have zero callers. Records whose plan/funding never produces a report are never re-hashed after finalize, so storage drift on them is never detected (they stay SIGNED). The helper itself is sound: CAS on status IN (SIGNED,REPORTED)+deletedAt null, custody + security event in one tx, idempotent.

findings.dataFlow: member B (evidence.create) -> POST /v1/uploads/sessions {teamId, evidenceId of A's SIGNED record, targetPartIndex: 999, originalFileName} -> initiate -> PUT parts -> complete {verifyHash:true} -> evidence_parts row with server sha256 on A's signed record -> /public/verify and authenticated views list it as part of the signed record -> next report job re-hashes ALL parts, composite != fileSha256 -> rejectEvidenceIntegrity -> FAILED_HASH_MISMATCH (terminal, no recovery path).

findings.blastRadius: Every SIGNED/REPORTED record in every team workspace; any member with evidence.create (typically ordinary members) can target colleagues' records. Personal workspaces unaffected (only the owner is a member).
findings.impact: Content injection into a signed record visible publicly and in reviewer surfaces with a server-computed hash beside it; permanent destruction of a record's verifiability (FAILED_HASH_MISMATCH cannot be reversed, recovery is re-capture). For records whose plan never generates a report, the injected part persists indefinitely with no detection.

findings.observed: Status is validated in phase A (reserve) only. Phase B renders and publishes the PDF outside any lock (seconds to minutes). Phase C re-checks only the reservation row and the version slot, then unconditionally writes status REPORTED and verificationStatus, and appends custody events. The only repair is the client calling /complete again (alreadyFinalized path re-applies retention when storageObjectLockMode is null). OTS and first-report reconcilers eventually cover those two, but no code re-applies retention or writes the missing custody outcome; the lifecycle contract's claim 'reconciled by governance services' has no implementation (grep of applyDefaultObjectRetention shows only the complete path).
findings.expected: Post-commit steps are durable intents (outbox/job) retried until recorded, and the response for a committed SIGNED record reports success-with-pending-protection rather than an error.
findings.dataFlow: commit SIGNED -> PutObjectRetention throws (e.g. transient 503) -> 5xx to client -> row SIGNED, storage_object_lock_mode NULL, custody chain lacks a lock outcome.
findings.rootCause: Side effects after commit executed inline with no retry owner.
findings.blastRadius: Any finalize during an S3 hiccup where the client does not retry (mobile/intake contributors that treat 5xx as failure).
findings.impact: Records show 'storage needs review' indefinitely and their custody chain never states whether protection applied; users see a failed upload for a record that is actually sealed (may re-capture, creating duplicates).
findings.reproduction: Make PutObjectRetention fail once (MinIO policy or fault injection) and call /complete once.
findings.runtimeProofIdea: Unit/integration test with storage double throwing on applyDefaultObjectRetention; assert row state and custody events; then run all reconcilers and assert nothing records the lock outcome.
findings.remediation: Enqueue a durable 'apply-retention-and-record' job keyed by evidence id inside the finalize tx (or reconcile SIGNED rows with null lock snapshot and no lock custody outcome); return 200 with protection pending.
findings.acceptanceProof: Fault-injection test: lock outcome eventually recorded without client retry.
findings.migrationBackfill: Select SIGNED/REPORTED rows with storage_object_lock_mode IS NULL and no EVIDENCE_LOCKED/STORAGE_PROTECTION_UNAVAILABLE custody event; re-run the snapshot.

findings.title: Finalize streams/hashes all originals and calls the TSA inside a 120s DB transaction, and checks the size limit only after hashing parts; large resumable uploads (sessions allow 50 GiB, evidence max 1 GiB) can never finalize and every retry re-reads the whole object

evidence.snippet: const sha256 = await sha256HexFromStream(body as unknown as Readable);

findings.observed: In the parts branch each part is HEADed, fully streamed and hashed, and only then is the summed size compared to readMaxEvidenceSizeBytes (the single-file branch checks before hashing). All of it plus signing and up to three 20s TSA subprocess calls must finish within the 120s interactive-transaction timeout while holding a pooled connection and the evidence advisory lock. When exceeded, Prisma rolls back; the row stays UPLOADING; no terminal/abandoned state exists, so the client's retries repeat the full download.
findings.expected: Size bounds enforced from HEAD before any GET; hashing and TSA performed outside the DB transaction (hash first, then a short claim tx that re-verifies the VersionId); upload-session byte cap aligned with the evidence cap.
findings.dataFlow: resumable session (<=50 GiB) -> /complete -> tx: GET+hash GBs -> timeout -> rollback -> 500 -> retry -> same.
findings.rootCause: Network/CPU-bound work inside an interactive transaction; inconsistent size limits.
findings.blastRadius: Large video captures / multi-part packages near or above the cap; connection-pool pressure for all API traffic during finalize storms.
findings.impact: Permanently unfinalizable records with uploaded bytes and no cleanup; repeated full-object egress per retry.
findings.reproduction: Upload a 3 GiB object through a resumable session and call /complete; observe transaction timeout rather than EVIDENCE_TOO_LARGE.
findings.runtimeProofIdea: Local MinIO + PG: session with a 2 GiB object; time the /complete; assert error code.
findings.remediation: Check Σ HEAD sizes before streaming; move hashing/TSA before the tx and bind by VersionId; cap MAX_TOTAL_BYTES at readMaxEvidenceSizeBytes().
findings.acceptanceProof: Oversize finalize returns 413 without any GET; finalize of a max-size object succeeds with the tx lasting < 1s.

findings.title: Integrity re-hash (FAILED_HASH_MISMATCH gate) runs only inside report generation; records without report entitlement are never re-verified, and the declared reconciler/completion sources are dead
findings.observed: grep for rejectEvidenceIntegrity finds exactly two callers, both in prepareReportArtifacts. No periodic or on-demand integrity re-hash exists; 'worker.reconciler' and 'api.completion' have zero callers.
findings.expected: An entitlement-independent integrity re-verification (sampled or scheduled) so that storage drift on any record reaches FAILED_HASH_MISMATCH and the verify page.
findings.dataFlow: FREE record -> SIGNED -> no report job -> bytes never re-hashed -> verify page keeps showing 'Signed' + stored hash.
findings.rootCause: Hard gate was attached to the report pipeline, which is commercially gated.
findings.blastRadius: All records that never generate a report.
findings.impact: Integrity status is only as fresh as the last report; unverified drift is invisible.
findings.reproduction: Finalize a record without report entitlement, overwrite the object version out of band (legacy row without VersionId), observe status stays SIGNED indefinitely.
findings.remediation: Add an integrity reconciler (bounded batch, VersionId-pinned re-hash) that calls rejectEvidenceIntegrity with source worker.reconciler; remove dead source labels otherwise.
findings.acceptanceProof: Reconciler test flips a drifted non-reported record to FAILED_HASH_MISMATCH.
findings.ownerDecision: Whether integrity re-verification of non-reported records is a product commitment.

findings.title: Evidence library status maps (web + mobile mirror) render FAILED_HASH_MISMATCH as a neutral 'Status not recorded'; UPLOADED is a dead enum still driving UI copy and probes
findings.observed: The canonical library label/tone functions (used by EvidenceLibraryRow and QueueSelectionPreview) have no FAILED_HASH_MISMATCH case; the mobile mirror copies that gap while another mobile module labels it 'Integrity failed'. Multiple modules compute 'ready/needs report' independently (home-view-model.ts:3109, evidence-library-alerts.ts:61, mobile evidence-library.ts:329). UPLOADED is never written yet is filterable and labelled 'Needs report' on Home.
findings.expected: One shared status-presentation authority (e.g. packages/shared-evidence-presentation) covering every enum value, with FAILED_HASH_MISMATCH as danger.
findings.dataFlow: API status FAILED_HASH_MISMATCH -> getRecordStatusLabel default branch -> neutral chip.
findings.rootCause: Enum value added (Phase A0) without updating the frontend switch statements; mirrors hand-copied.
findings.blastRadius: Every integrity-failed record in library/queue views.
findings.impact: Integrity failure presented as a missing value; reviewers can miss it in lists.
findings.reproduction: Set a record to FAILED_HASH_MISMATCH and open /evidence.
findings.remediation: Add the case to the shared map, delete mirrors in favour of the shared module, drop UPLOADED from filters/probes (or document it as legacy).
findings.acceptanceProof: Exhaustive-switch type test over Prisma EvidenceStatus in the shared map.

findings.title: Direct-capture discard releases a reservation with an unguarded update(WHERE id) after reading status without the evidence lock; it can soft-delete a record that concurrently became SIGNED and append a false 'no content committed' custody event

evidence.snippet: await tx.evidence.update({ where: { id: evidence.id }, data: { deletedAt: now }, });

findings.observed: Completion holds the EVIDENCE advisory lock, discard holds the CAPTURE-SESSION lock; they do not serialize. If discard's status read occurs after completion's finalize updateMany but before its commit, READ COMMITTED lets discard's later update (WHERE id) apply deletedAt to the now-SIGNED row. Most interleavings instead deadlock (custody append takes the evidence lock) and one side aborts.
findings.expected: Discard takes the evidence advisory lock and uses updateMany WHERE status IN (CREATED, UPLOADING) AND deletedAt IS NULL.
findings.dataFlow: complete: updateMany SIGNED (uncommitted) -> discard reads UPLOADING -> complete commits -> discard update deletedAt -> custody EVIDENCE_DELETED after SIGNATURE_APPLIED.
findings.rootCause: Different lock keys for the two writers of the same row.
findings.blastRadius: Direct-capture (UC-0..UC-5) records whose client discards while a /complete is in flight (e.g. after client timeout).
findings.impact: Sealed evidence disappears from active surfaces with a contradictory custody statement; with deletedAt set and no deleteScheduledForUtc the trash-grace boundary does not delay destruction eligibility (Object Lock retention still blocks when enabled).
findings.reproduction: Interleave as described with a breakpoint in completeEvidence after the claim.
findings.runtimeProofIdea: Two-connection PG test driving the two transactions with explicit pauses.
findings.remediation: Acquire pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext(evidenceId)) in discard before reading, and make the update conditional.
findings.migrationBackfill: Query evidence where status IN ('SIGNED','REPORTED') AND deleted_at IS NOT NULL AND lifecycle_state='ACTIVE'.

findings.title: Abandoned uploads are never cleaned: stuck CREATED/UPLOADING rows have no terminal state, orphan-scan is read-only, multipart reaper runs only via external cron call, and a lost initiate race leaks an untracked S3 multipart

evidence.snippet: First pass intentionally does NOT delete anything.
await client.$executeRawUnsafe( `UPDATE "evidence_upload_sessions" SET "state" = 'UPLOADING', "multipart_upload_id" = $3, ... AND "multipart_upload_id" IS NULL`,

findings.observed: No code moves stale CREATED/UPLOADING evidence to any state or deletes its objects; the only multipart abort sweeper is DB-driven and only armed by POST /v1/ops/reconcile; if the initiate UPDATE matches 0 rows it returns 0 (no throw), so the compensating AbortMultipartUpload in the catch never runs and the UploadId is recorded nowhere. No AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload lifecycle rule exists in the repo.
findings.expected: A terminal ABANDONED path for evidence plus prefix cleanup (subject to Object Lock), and an infrastructure bucket rule for incomplete multipart uploads.
findings.dataFlow: create -> PUT bytes -> never complete -> object retained indefinitely (locked if Object Lock on).
findings.rootCause: Reconciliation deliberately read-only; no owner decision on abandonment.
findings.impact: Storage cost and retained customer bytes with no product-visible record; stuck rows count in operations probes.
findings.reproduction: Create evidence, upload, never complete; after 30 days object and row remain.
findings.runtimeProofIdea: grep proof: no writer transitions CREATED/UPLOADING except finalize.
findings.remediation: Owner decision on abandonment TTL; implement abandon transition + trash; check the initiate UPDATE row count and abort on 0; add bucket lifecycle rule in infra.
findings.acceptanceProof: Abandonment job test + infra config review.
findings.migrationBackfill: Inventory evidence in CREATED/UPLOADING older than N days.
findings.ownerDecision: Abandonment TTL and whether abandoned bytes may be deleted.

questions.q: Do evidence presigned PUTs on the Object Lock bucket succeed when the client omits both checksumSha256Base64 and contentMd5Base64? S3 requires Content-MD5 or an x-amz-checksum header for PutObject with Object Lock parameters, and presignPutObject signs lock params unconditionally when S3_OBJECT_LOCK_ENABLED while checksum is optional (params.checksumSha256Base64 ?? null). Same question for UploadPart under a lock-configured CreateMultipartUpload (no checksum signed).
